Arguments supporting the bail application are The investigation having been completed, there is no justification in denying him bail. The incident was in 2015, and the present investigating officer was in charge for over two years. The applicant was questioned numerous times and found to have nothing to do with the murder. Arguments opposing the bail application are The investigating officer was able to crack the case only after several years due to the ingenuity of the applicant. The scientific evidence and the report of the fingerprint expert clearly link the applicant with the crime. The offence was committed in a brutal manner, and a person such as the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. After the incident, the applicant had gone abroad, and if released on bail, there is a chance that he would evade and make himself scarce.

Whatever was done was under the influence of liquor and due to quarrel between the husband and wife. In support of his submissions, he relied on the case of Bhaurao Abaji Dhandre vs. State of Maharashtra, reported in 2001 ALL MR (Cri) 1730. Section 323 IPC: Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt: Whoever, except in the case provided for by section334, voluntarily causes hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
